title: Review the spec
why: Three build briefs that must each stand alone; the review checks their claims against the engine (Event and Clan literals, every caller of World::run past the end, cross-build's endTurn loop, map-view's pointer handling) and that the decisions match founding.md.

title: Civs, phases and the pick in the engine
why: The shapes are fixed in the spec (Civ, Phase, the civs step, ChooseCiv, joining and levy rules), so the work is careful plumbing across world, clans, markets, pregame and the CLI without changing the pre-game; many small tests on hand-built worlds.

title: Units: making, feeding, moving and disbanding
why: A Dijkstra with predecessors, labour banking, hunger and disbanding, all specified with exact rules and tie-breaks; plus a scripted lead game mirrored in Rust and JS for cross-build, which needs care but no new design.

title: The page: pick, top bar, selection panel and orders
why: Plain-JS UI work on #31's page (a pick card, a selection panel with buttons, right-click moves, drawing civs, units and routes, feed kinds) checked by check.mjs and headless Chrome screenshots; many details, no hard algorithms, as #31's page step was.

title: Review the piece
why: Checks founding.md bullet by bullet and the unchanged pre-game, then plays founding and a warrior's life through the page only with headless Chrome clicks and right-clicks, reading screenshots, as #31's review did well on sonnet high.
